name: Cocktail Glass
baseMeaning: A stemmed cocktail glass, signaling fancy-coded unwind, social-coded affection, or cocktail appreciation.
tldr: 🍸 usually turns a sentence into a stylish drink plan, date invitation, or affectionate sign-off after a good time.

contextMeanings.meaning: It refers to an actual mixed drink or cocktail in a stemmed glass.
As a sign-off, it suggests a good night out or affectionate social energy without spelling out what happened.
contextMeanings.example: you would have loved that place 🍸

contextMeanings.meaning: It can suggest a stylish, relatively new drinking spot and turn a casual invitation into a date.
It can mark an after-work drink or team celebration rather than a request to drink during the working day.
contextMeanings.example: the report is filed, team drinks on me thursday 🍸

platformNotes.note: In a direct iMessage, ending with 🍸 makes a plan feel friendly and specific without listing every detail. Adding a time or question mark makes it easier for the recipient to answer.
In an Instagram story or caption, 🍸 can label a cocktail-bar visit or close a drinks-related post. It often feels more atmospheric than like a firm invitation unless a date or place appears nearby.
In TikTok captions and comments, 🍸 commonly accompanies clips of cocktail bars and stylish night-out places. It describes the atmosphere more readily than it commits either person to a time.
In Slack, 🍸 works best in an after-work or social channel; in a general project thread, it can look like a stray reaction. A concrete time and location keeps the drink plan from being just the emoji.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z often treats 🍸 as the quick, trendy alternative to 🍷: meeting at a newer bar or signaling a fresh, less formal date.
Millennials may use 🍸 in friendly messages about meeting for drinks or enjoying a night out, without intending every use to be romantic.
Gen X recipients may first take 🍸 literally as an actual cocktail, so the possible dating invitation can take a moment to notice.

warnings.title: Friend hang that sounds like a date
warnings.description: 🍸 can suggest a newer, more intimate outing, while 🍻 is the default for friends. If the hang is deliberately casual, use 🍻 or name the group.

warnings.title: Expecting a long dinner
warnings.description: 🍸 points toward a quick cocktail at a newer venue, while 🍷 better signals hours at a table. Choose 🍷 when the plan is meant to unfold slowly.

seoDescription: What does 🍸 mean? It often signals a stylish cocktail, a social night out, or a slightly flirty invitation to meet for a drink.

longForm.overview:
The 🍸 is a stemmed cocktail glass, and it usually does something quieter than naming a literal beverage. Put it at the end of a sentence and the sentence becomes a plan: “meet me for a drink,” “we are having a night out,” or “that was a good cocktail.” It can also carry friendly affection after a good update, which is why it feels more social than merely informational.

It differs from its neighbours in the kind of outing it suggests. 🍸 points toward a quick, trendy drink at a newer venue, while 🍷 points toward a slower date built around sitting across a table for hours. 🍻 is the easier choice for a casual friend hang. The glass’s dressiness matters: 🍸 can make an invitation feel dressed up without committing to the long, intimate mood of wine. It works especially well as closing punctuation: the image softens the ask while leaving the venue and time open.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
The usual home for 🍸 is the end of an invitation or a reaction. “cocktails after work? 🍸” asks for a drink without spelling out every logistical detail; “we earned one tonight 🍸” marks a shared good moment. In dating threads, the glass can quietly turn a vague “want to hang?” into a more specific drink date.

It is also used when someone is naming the drink itself: “that grapefruit cocktail was so good 🍸.” Among friends, it can work as a light, affectionate sign-off after news, plans, or congratulations, though it may sound more dressed up than a casual group hang.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
🍸 can misfire when the sender means an ordinary drink with friends. Because the glass is stylish and often points to a newer venue, some recipients may hear a date invitation where none was intended; 🍻 is the safer choice for a casual friend hang. The reverse mistake is choosing 🍸 for an evening meant to unfold slowly over several hours: 🍷 fits that kind of sit-down date better.

Also avoid adding 🍸 to a sober, alcohol-free, or work-focused message unless a cocktail is literally what you are discussing. In a serious conversation, the festive drink image can feel off-topic. If the goal is the plan, add a time and place; if it is appreciation for the beverage, name the cocktail.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone ends a message with 🍸, a simple “yes, 7?” or “i’m in 🍸” keeps the invitation moving. Mirror the emoji when you want the reply to feel warm and social; ask for a time and place when you genuinely need to settle the plan. There is no need to explain what the glass means.

If the message came from a guy and you are unsure whether it is a date, answer plainly rather than copying the ambiguity: “friend drink or date drink?” That question can sound blunt, but it prevents a quick cocktail invite from becoming an awkward assumption later. If they chose 🍸 because they truly enjoyed the drink, simple appreciation for the cocktail also works.

faqs.question: What does 🍸 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: It usually means he is suggesting or mentioning a stylish cocktail. In a dating thread, it often doubles as an invitation to meet for a drink at a newer place.

faqs.question: Is 🍸 flirty
faqs.answer: Often, yes, especially in a dating thread. Among friends it can simply mark a night out, so the surrounding message matters more than the emoji alone.

faqs.question: What does 🍸 mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it usually labels a cocktail, a stylish bar, or the atmosphere of a night out. It can suggest an invitation, but it is not necessarily tied to a specific plan unless a time or location appears.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🍸 and 🍷
faqs.answer: 🍸 suggests a quicker, trendier cocktail at a newer venue, while 🍷 suggests a slower evening spent sitting across a table. For a casual friend hang, 🍻 is usually the safer choice.

conversationExamples.message: there’s a new cocktail bar near the station, thursday? 🍸
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is an invitation for a stylish drink date, probably with the venue left open for the other person to influence. Reply with a time, suggest another place, or say you cannot make it.

conversationExamples.message: friday survived, i need a cocktail 🍸
conversationExamples.interpretation: The glass is mainly a playful sign-off after shared stress. A friend may answer with their own exhaustion or turn it into an actual plan, though 🍻 would make the group invitation more explicit.

conversationExamples.message: the report is filed, team drinks on me thursday 🍸
conversationExamples.interpretation: This proposes an after-work drink to mark the finished task, not drinking during work hours. Confirm whether you are coming rather than responding to the emoji alone.

conversationExamples.message: dad, what should i order you for dinner? 🍸
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here the glass refers to an actual cocktail and asks for a recommendation. If alcohol is not appropriate, name the drinks you will both be having instead.

conversationExamples.message: just found the cutest little cocktail bar 🍸
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji expresses cocktail appreciation and invites shared excitement about the place. Respond with another photo, a drink recommendation, or a suggestion to visit together.
